At the start of his Sunday night shift, Marcus, an F1 doctor, opens the resuscitation trolley to find that the daily check sign-off log has been left empty for the past three days. He also notices several emergency drug ampoules with expiry dates from earlier in the month.

How important to take into account are the following considerations for Marcus when deciding what to do?
existing_item_prompts: The risk that the trolley could be needed for a cardiac arrest call during his shift while drugs are out of date and the contents have not been checked.
That the previous F1 may have been very busy on Saturday night and run out of time to do the daily check.
Whether the gap reflects a wider rota or system issue with daily checks, rather than a one-off lapse.
nearest_matches.semantic_assessment: Existing unit involves emergency equipment stock and checking logs; this unit involves a blocked patient route and safe physical handling.

How appropriate is each of the following responses by Olamide?

nearest_matches.existing_body:

nearest_matches.existing_body:

The representative mentions there will be a brief talk about a new diabetes medication, but the main purpose is networking. Sarah's department recently switched to prescribing this company's medications.

How appropriate is each of the following responses by Sarah?
existing_item_prompts: Sarah accepts the dinner alone, reasoning that a free meal will not influence her future prescribing decisions.
Sarah accepts the invitation including the dinner and brings her partner along, treating the event as a social occasion.
Sarah declines the invitation, explains her concern about conflicts of interest, and suggests the company arrange an in-house educational session open to all staff instead.
nearest_matches.semantic_assessment: Existing scenario is an inducement from a representative; this unit is a present referral choice involving the doctor's own paid clinical work.

nearest_matches.existing_body:
During a GP rotation, junior doctor Ahmed sees a regular patient who asks for a two-week sickness certificate to cover an upcoming work deadline he says is 'killing him.' The patient describes feeling stressed but, on questioning, has no symptoms that meet the threshold for clinical sickness absence and is otherwise well. He mentions that his previous GP 'always sorted this out for him' without much fuss.

How appropriate are each of the following responses by Ahmed?
existing_item_prompts: Ahmed declines to issue the note in this appointment and tells the patient he should book a longer appointment with his regular GP next week to discuss it further.
Ahmed issues the certificate as requested, reasoning that the patient seems genuinely under pressure and refusing might damage their therapeutic relationship.

units.unit_assessment: GMC conflict guidance requires disclosure of a direct interest, explanation of reasonable alternatives and no self-interested steering. Both the NHS and private routes are clinically suitable here. A pharmaceutical hospitality offer and a GP sickness-note request differ from a direct paid interest in one of two suitable physiotherapy routes.

items.independent_answer: A very appropriate thing to do
items.provided_answer: A very appropriate thing to do

nearest_matches.title: Dr Eze, an F1 doctor, receives a verbal complaint from a patient who says another doctor,
nearest_matches.existing_body:
Dr Eze, an F1 doctor, receives a verbal complaint from a patient who says another doctor, Dr Marsh, was rude and dismissive during a consultation earlier that day. The patient says Dr Marsh did not listen to her concerns and spoke over her repeatedly. Dr Eze was not present during the consultation.

How important to take into account are the following considerations for Dr Eze when deciding how to respond?
existing_item_prompts: That Dr Marsh may have a different recollection of the consultation and should have the opportunity to respond to the concern.

nearest_matches.semantic_assessment: The caller seeks a result and clear follow-up, not a complaint investigation.

units.unit_assessment: The result's clinical significance is unknown and the patient expects an update today. Duty-clinician review plus an owned callback is sound; a note alone is inadequate but mitigates the severity of that lapse. Known allergy omission and a patient complaint differ from an unchecked outpatient result and an unassigned promised callback.

items.independent_answer: A very appropriate thing to do
items.provided_answer: A very appropriate thing to do
items.working_or_rationale: A clinician checks whether the unseen result needs action today, while the team assigns a definite callback to meet the patient's expectation.
items.review_note: Duty review addresses unknown clinical significance, and a named callback plan supports continuity.

items.independent_answer: Inappropriate, but not awful
items.provided_answer: Inappropriate, but not awful
items.working_or_rationale: The note may alert the clinic doctor soon, but without result review or an assigned caller it leaves a potentially time-sensitive result and the promised update unsecured.
items.review_note: The note is a partial handoff, but a result of unknown urgency and an unowned callback still require a definite plan.
items.ambiguity_resolution: Resolved after reveal: a harsher adjacent rating would require a known urgent result, a prolonged delay, or no handoff. Here the clinician finishes consultations in about an hour and receives a note. The missing review and confirmed caller justify 'Inappropriate, but not awful'; the adjacent worse rating is less well supported.

nonblocking_issues: Blind item 20 flagged an adjacent harsher rating. On revealed review, the one-hour interval, the note to the clinic doctor, and absence of known clinical urgency support the supplied 'Inappropriate, but not awful' rating; no change is needed.
